// debounce.ts
export function debounce(fn: (...args: any[]) => void, waitMs: number) {
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    return (...args: any[]) => {
        if (timer !== null) {
            return; // already scheduled
        }
        timer = setTimeout(() => fn(args), waitMs);
        timer = null;
    };
}

The intended behavior: debounce(fn, waitMs) returns a function that delays calling fn until
waitMs milliseconds have passed since the LAST call, passing through the latest arguments,
and cancelling any pending call when a new one arrives.

and add a small self-test that runs when the file is executed directly and prints "all tests passed".

## Bug Analysis

The current implementation has a critical flaw:

```typescript
timer = setTimeout(() => fn(args), waitMs);
timer = null; // ← BUG: resets timer immediately after scheduling
```

Since `timer` is set to `null` immediately after scheduling a new `setTimeout`, any subsequent call will see `timer === null` and schedule yet another timer — **never cancelling the previous one**. The "cancel pending call when a new one arrives" requirement is never met.

**The fix:** Use `clearTimeout(timer)` to cancel the previous timer, and only reset `timer = null` when the timer actually fires.

// debounce.ts
export function debounce(fn: (...args: any[]) => void, waitMs: number) {
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    return (...args: any[]) => {
        if (timer !== null) {
            return; // already scheduled
        }
        timer = setTimeout(() => fn(args), waitMs);
        timer = null;
    };
}

The intended behavior: debounce(fn, waitMs) returns a function that delays calling fn until
waitMs milliseconds have passed since the LAST call, passing through the latest arguments,
and cancelling any pending call when a new one arrives.
